attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, in his own voice.

semantics.note: Keeps the and/or disjunction and the 'largest customers' scope. Dropping 'explicitly' is a small softening but does not change what can be tested. This is a present-state observation.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair. The disjunction is read as he wrote it. 'Discussing dropping' read as cutting usage is ordinary, and his own examples (Grok, Muse, the Meta/Microsoft reports) match. The window up to the post date is reasonable.

evidence.note: Press reports name SpaceX and Microsoft as the two customers behind about a fifth of H1 2026 revenue. Published before the evaluation date.
SpaceX owns xAI/Grok and Cursor and competes directly with Anthropic in models and coding tools.
The Information, via Investing.com: Meta and Microsoft are cutting internal Claude use and steering staff to in-house tools. Meta is building Muse Code.
Microsoft's resale of Claude is growing, so it is not dropping Anthropic entirely. Under the disjunction and the cut-in-use reading this limits the claim but does not contradict it.

reviews.rationale: The two largest reported customers fit: SpaceX owns rival Grok and Cursor, and Microsoft is cutting internal Claude use for its own tools. Meta is also cutting use and building Muse. No one has fully exited, and Microsoft's resale is growing, but the disjunctive claim holds. Meta's rank among top customers is less firmly sourced in the packet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: Keeps 'majority of', 'non-cancellable' and 'over $430 billion'. The sarcastic motive ('so confident') is rightly left out. The timing parts are checkable against S-1 data.

contract.note: The plain readings are ordinary. Blank Q3 dollar statements count as leaving out the majority. Commitments are summed from the S-1. 'Kick in' means most capacity starts after the period. 'Slow' means Q3 growth below Q2's. None is stretched.

evidence.note: Close reading of the S-1: statements run to June 30 and Q3 dollars are blank. Q3 revenue appears only as a multiple, along with a few operating metrics.
Derived Q3 growth of about 45-48% against 144.2% in Q2, the first quarter to add fewer dollars. Growth slowed.
Google, Amazon, Microsoft and Broadcom non-cancellable deals sum to about $430.6bn. Most Broadcom capacity comes online from 2027. The filing warns growth will decline.
$321.4bn of leases had not begun at June end, starting 2026-2028, which supports 'before... kick in'.

reviews.rationale: Every graded part holds on secondary readings of the S-1. Financials stop at Q2 and Q3 dollars are blank. Non-cancellable deals total about $430.6bn, just over $430bn. Most new capacity starts from 2027. Q3 growth (about 45-48%) fell well below Q2 (144%). Limits: some Q3 metrics and part of the cloud spend already exist, and the S-1 itself was not read directly.
